column1: # ZAP baseline scan triage for the secure DB access gateway edge.
# Format is ZAP's own -c format: id<TAB>LEVEL<TAB>justification, one per line,
# at least three tab-separated fields. A malformed line makes zap-baseline.py
# exit 3, so keep it strictly tab-separated. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# Rules NOT listed here keep ZAP's default level of WARN, and `fail_action: true`
# turns any WARN into a failed build. That is deliberate: only alerts we have
# consciously decided about are listed, so anything new still blocks. Do not
# bulk-ignore rule ids here; add a line only with a written justification.
# The action reads this file a second time to decide whether to pass -c at all.
# Three facts about that reader, each checked against
# @zaproxy/actions-common-scans as pinned by action-baseline v0.14.0 (^1.3.0):
#   * `-c` is passed only when at least one line has a second field of exactly
#     IGNORE, so a file with no IGNORE lines is not applied at all. That, and
#     not a malformed line, is the silent-loss mode worth guarding against.
#   * `#` lines are skipped by both readers, so this header is safe.
#   * A non-comment line with fewer than three tab-separated fields is loud,
#     not silent: zap-baseline.py's load_config raises ValueError and the job
#     exits 3 (see the format note above), failing the build.
# Ids must be the base rule id, never a sub-id such as `10055-6`:
# zap-baseline.py passes every id to int() when it builds the automation plan,
# and a sub-id makes the scan exit non-zero before it starts.
# 10015 - Re-examine Cache-control Directives (Informational)
#   Fires whenever caching directives are missing or inconsistent, so it cannot
#   tell a regression apart from a clean `no-store`. The edge serves a single
#   Cache-Control: no-store and hides the upstream copy in every proxy
#   location, and ZAP's own remedy - `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` - is
#   weaker than that. Nothing to change; it is a review prompt, not a defect.

column3: Cache directives are set deliberately: the edge serves a single no-store, the upstream copy is hidden, and ZAP's suggested directives are weaker than that. Not a defect.

column1: # 10016 - Web Browser XSS Protection Not Enabled
#   The X-XSS-Protection header is deliberately not set. It is deprecated and
#   removed from modern browsers, and its audit filter has itself been an XSS
#   vector; the Content-Security-Policy header on this edge is the control that
#   replaces it. Recorded in SECURITY.md as an intentional omission.

column3: X-XSS-Protection is intentionally not set; it is deprecated and superseded by the Content-Security-Policy header (see SECURITY.md).

column1: # 10027 - Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments (Informational)
#   False positive in the minified SPA bundle: ZAP treats React's quoted SVG
#   namespace URL (`http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`) as a comment, then matches the
#   SQL editor's ordinary `SELECT` completion keyword later on the same line.
#   Neither string is a source comment or discloses internal information.

column3: ZAP mistakes the quoted React SVG namespace URL for a comment and matches the SQL editor's normal SELECT completion token later on the same minified line; neither is a comment or sensitive disclosure.

column1: # 10049 - Content Cacheability (reported as Non-Storable Content, x6)
#   The rule has exactly three outcomes - non-storable, storable but not
#   cacheable, storable and cacheable - and it alerts on all three, so no
#   Cache-Control value clears it. Non-storable is the intended result for the
#   API and the SPA shell, which is what no-store at the edge produces.

column3: Content Cacheability alerts on every possible cache state, so no header clears it; the state it reported (non-storable) is the intended one for this edge.

column1: # 10055 - CSP (reported as style-src unsafe-inline, x3)
#   Only the style-src sub-alert fired. Inline styles are an accepted risk,
#   recorded as W-3 in THREAT_MODEL.md. script-src - the half that turns an
#   injected tag into execution - is exactly 'self' or 'none' in all three
#   served policies, and the "Verify served CSP script-src and edge/app header
#   parity" step in the security-exception-policy job fails the build if any of
#   them widens, so that half is not left to this suppression.

column3: Only style-src unsafe-inline fired, an accepted risk (THREAT_MODEL W-3); script-src stays exactly 'self' or 'none' and a CI assertion in the security-exception-policy job blocks any widening.

column1: # 10109 - Modern Web Application (Informational)
#   Detection that the target looks like a modern SPA, raised because links use
#   _self. ZAP's own solution text says no changes are required.

column3: Informational detection that the target is a modern SPA; ZAP states no changes are required.

column1: # 10116 - ZAP is Out of Date (Medium)
#   Describes the scanner build, not the target. The image is pinned by digest so
#   upgrades happen as reviewed changes, and bumping that digest is independent
#   of anything this application can change.

column3: Describes the pinned scanner build rather than the target; the digest is bumped in a reviewed change, not by this application.

column1: # 90004 - Insufficient Site Isolation Against Spectre Vulnerability
#   Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy was `same-site`, which this rule rejects: it
#   accepts only `same-origin` or `cross-origin`. Fixed at the source in
#   nginx/nginx.conf, auth0_api/app/middleware/setup.py and
#   sql_query_api/app_factory.py rather than suppressed. Deliberately absent from
#   the lines above - if it fires again a security header has regressed and the
#   build should go red.
